shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on weathered coarse stone
monolithic upright stone block/pillar as the carrying surface
horizontal band or register of repeated figures near the top
a circular element (disc on A; round drilled hole on B)
raised bands/ridges bounding the carved zone
justification: Both are monolithic stone blocks whose surfaces carry very shallow, rounded low relief organised into a horizontal band of repeated curvilinear figures across the upper zone, and both show a conspicuous circular feature below that band. But A is an anthropomorphic statue with a modelled head, shoulders, arms and belt-like bands governing the whole composition, whereas B is a plain rectangular block bearing only a frieze of quadruped-like creatures, so the overall schemes and the subject matter diverge sharply.
